- Overestimate prices in bullish sentiment periods, especially when sentiment is >0.5 and recent prices are rising.
- Underestimate prices after sharp spikes or corrections when sentiment is negative or near-zero.
- Avoid over-optimism in 30-day forecasts when sentiment has recently dipped below 0.3 — model tends to overshoot recovery.
- Correct for mean reversion bias: if 10-day average of true prices is significantly lower than forecast, reduce forecast by 5–10%.
- When sentiment is volatile (e.g., alternating +0.3 to -0.2), reduce forecast volatility and anchor to recent 7-day average.
- For forecasts with early spikes, reduce peak values by 5–10% if sentiment is weak or negative in the following 3 days.
- If true outcome is consistently below forecast for 3+ consecutive days, adjust downward by 2–5% per day until sentiment stabilizes.
